question: In the morning, Diane's food truck had 198 orders logged, tracked over 120 minutes, or 2 hours, of breakfast service. By midday, 59 more orders came in. In the afternoon, 16 more orders were logged. By evening, six other food trucks at the festival pooled their order counts equally with hers, making the total seven times as large. Finally, 920 orders were fulfilled and closed out, leaving Diane with far more open orders than her competitor Hank, who only had 50. How many orders did Diane have left open?

A stadium sold 209 season passes in the first hour, even though the stadium has a dozen entry gates. Eight more matching sales hours followed, making the total nine times as large. A batch of 1,464 passes was refunded due to a schedule change. A late sales push added 73 more passes. Finally, 75 more passes were sold at the box office. How many season passes were sold in total?

A thrift store had 146 sweaters on the rack, priced at 14,600 cents combined. A morning sale sold 25 of them. A donation drop-off added 59 more. An afternoon sale sold 77 more. A clearance event sold 52 more. Finally, a large donation added 73 more sweaters. How many sweaters were on the rack at the end?

In the morning, Marcus had 109 points in a school reading challenge. By midday, he earned 32 more points finishing a chapter book. In the afternoon, he earned 32 more points for a book report. Later, a bonus quiz added 57 more points. By evening, 90 points were deducted for a late submission. A second deduction removed 12 more points. Finally, a school-wide bonus made his total nine times as large, putting him far ahead of his classmate Theo, who only had 200 points. How many points did Marcus end up with?

Two rival lemonade stands compared earnings. Mia's stand had $22 in the cash box, counted over 60 minutes, or 1 hour, of the first shift. Two more matching helpers pooled their earnings in, tripling the total. A summer storm cost her $26 in ruined supplies. A big group of customers then added $70. Finally, seven more matching stands joined a street fair pool, making the total eight times as large, far more than her rival Kayla's $200. How much money did Mia end up with?

A school had 32 trophies in its display case, even though the school has 15 sports teams. A matching donation doubled the case's count. A late addition brought 3 more trophies. A regional tournament win tripled the total. Finally, a state championship sweep made the total five times as large. How many trophies were in the display case at the end?

In the morning, Ella had 43 dollars saved for a new bicycle. By midday, she earned 29 more dollars doing yard work. In the afternoon, seven more matching contributions from relatives made her total eight times as large. Later, three more matching gifts made it four times as large again. That evening, she split her savings evenly among 4 envelopes for different expenses and kept only one envelope going forward. A final matching bonus from her grandmother made that envelope's total four times as large. Finally, she added 36 more dollars from her piggy bank, ending up with far more than her friend Owen, who had only $200. How much money did Ella have in that envelope at the end?

In the morning, a printing press had 182 orders queued, logged over 60 minutes, or 1 hour, of intake. By midday, six more matching intake batches made the queue seven times as large. In the afternoon, 282 orders were completed and removed from the queue. By evening, six more matching intake batches made the queue seven times as large again. Finally, 6,660 orders were completed overnight. How many orders were left in the queue?

A grocery store had 145 crates of apples in the storeroom, even though the store has a dozen checkout lanes. A morning shipment took out 61 crates for the sales floor. An afternoon delivery brought in 78 more crates. A weekend rush used up 94 more crates. Finally, 59 more crates arrived from a late supplier. How many crates were left in the storeroom?

Two chess rivals compared their tournament points. Sasha had 130 points to start the season. She lost 5 points after a forfeited match. A club bonus, with three matching contributions, made her total four times as large. A rematch bonus then doubled her total. She earned 9 more points from a practice match. Finally, a season-ending championship made her total nine times as large, far ahead of her rival Petra, who only had 900 points. How many points did Sasha end up with?

In the morning, a moving company had 175 boxes to deliver, scheduled for 480 minutes, or 8 hours, of work, even though the crew has a dozen dollies. By midday, 79 more boxes were added from a second pickup. In the afternoon, 14 more boxes came from a third stop. By evening, seven more matching truckloads joined, making the total eight times as large. Finally, 248 boxes were delivered and removed from the count. How many boxes were left to deliver?

Two friends compared their savings for a trip. Noor had 39 dollars saved, even though the trip costs 500 dollars for the whole group. She earned 24 more dollars from a garage sale. She then split her savings evenly among 3 jars for different goals and kept only the travel jar going forward. Three more matching deposits made that jar four times as large. Finally, she split that jar evenly among 3 more expenses and kept only the plane ticket portion, ending up with less than her friend Dahlia. How much money did Noor have in the plane ticket portion?

Two rival museums compared their artifact collections. The City Museum had 209 artifacts cataloged. Four matching donations made the collection five times as large. Four more matching donations made it five times as large again. A local dig added 54 more artifacts. A university donation added 11 more. Finally, a national grant tripled the collection once more, leaving the City Museum with far more artifacts than the rival County Museum's 5,000. How many artifacts did the City Museum end up with?

In the morning, a movie theater had 112 empty seats before the first showing. By midday, 87 more seats filled up as customers arrived. In the afternoon, the theater added 76 more seats by opening an overflow section. Later, 66 more seats were added by opening a second overflow section. By evening, 12 more seats were added for a special late screening. How many seats did the theater have available by evening?

In the morning, a stadium had sold 180 tickets, counted over 60 minutes, or 1 hour, of the box office opening. By midday, two more matching sales hours tripled the total. In the afternoon, 39 more tickets sold. Later, 20 more tickets sold. By evening, seven more matching sales hours made the total eight times as large. Finally, 2,105 tickets were refunded due to a rain delay. How many tickets were still valid by the end of the day?

Two rival lemonade stands compared their day's cash. Theo's stand had $44 in the box, counted over 60 minutes, or 1 hour, of the morning. He earned $51 more from a busy crowd. Five more matching helpers pooled their earnings in, making the total six times as large. He earned $47 more from an afternoon rush. He earned $41 more from an evening crowd. He then paid $610 to his supplier for lemons and cups. Finally, he paid $29 for a permit renewal, ending with less than his rival stand run by Ivy, which made $100. How much money did Theo have left in the box?

In the morning, a school had 14 cans collected for the recycling drive, even though the school has 500 students enrolled. By midday, 16 more cans came in. In the afternoon, seven more matching classroom bins joined, making the total eight times as large. By evening, 75 more cans arrived from a neighborhood collection. Finally, 71 more cans came in from a late drop-off, and a citywide bonus made the total nine times as large. How many cans did the school collect in total?

In the morning, a farmers market had 128 baskets of strawberries, even though the market has 25 vendor tables. By midday, 38 more baskets arrived from a late farmer. In the afternoon, two more matching deliveries tripled the total. Later, 24 baskets were pulled for being overripe. By evening, 65 more baskets arrived from a final harvest. Finally, three more matching deliveries made the total four times as large. How many baskets of strawberries were at the market by the end of the day?

A toy store had 138 stuffed animals in a display, even though the store stocks a dozen animal types. The display was split evenly across 3 shelves, and only one shelf's animals were tracked going forward. A matching restock doubled that shelf's count. A late delivery added 6 more animals. Finally, 35 animals were sold during a weekend sale. How many stuffed animals were left on that shelf?

A farm had 169 chickens in the coop, even though the farm has 20 acres of land. A fox got into the coop and 43 chickens were lost. A breeding season tripled the remaining flock. The farm then split the flock evenly across 3 coops, and only one coop's chickens were counted going forward. Half of that coop's chickens were sold at auction, and only the remaining half stayed. Finally, three more matching coops joined, making that count four times as large. How many chickens were in that coop at the end?

Two friends compared their trading card totals. Farah had 34 cards, even though the shop carries 60 different sets, tracked over 60 minutes, or 1 hour, of trading. She lost 15 cards in a bad trade. A matching donation from a friend doubled her total. She then won 42 more cards in a tournament. A second tournament added 38 more. Finally, a grand prize added 76 more cards, leaving her with more cards than her friend Tomas, who had only 150. How many cards did Farah end up with?

In the morning, a fish tank had 17 guppies, even though the tank holds up to 100 fish. By midday, 4 fish were moved to a breeding tank. In the afternoon, 71 baby fish were added from a hatch. Later, 4 more fish were moved out for a school donation. By evening, 44 more fish were added from a second hatch. Finally, a matching second tank doubled the total. How many guppies were there by evening?

A garden had 78 sunflowers blooming, even though the garden has a dozen different flower beds. A storm destroyed 34 of them. A second planting doubled the remaining count. The flowers were then split evenly across 4 garden beds, and only one bed's flowers were counted going forward. Finally, 53 more sunflowers bloomed in that bed. How many sunflowers were in that bed at the end?

A charity had raised $239 by the first hour, tallied over 60 minutes, or 1 hour, of the telethon, even though 500 people tuned in. A second hour added $77 more. A third hour added $68 more. A fourth hour added $69 more. The charity then spent $188 on printing costs. Finally, $67 more was spent on shipping fees. How much money did the charity have left?

Two rival breweries compared barrel counts. Oakwood Brewery had 206 barrels aging, even though the cellar has a dozen sections. Five more matching cellars joined, making the total six times as large. A shipment removed 263 barrels for a big order. Seven more matching cellars joined, making it eight times as large. Three more matching cellars made it four times as large. Finally, five more matching cellars made it six times as large, leaving Oakwood far ahead of the rival Pinehill Brewery's 9,000 barrels. How many barrels did Oakwood Brewery end up with?
